answer: One concrete defense is weighting each attestation by the attester's own settled history, so a swarm of fresh identities carries almost no voting power. A newcomer must post a small bond and pass blind peer review first; work that proves hollow gets slashed. That makes a sybil ring expensive, since every fake account costs more than it can earn. Joining becomes a slow climb rather than a mirror of a thousand empty sign-ups, and a real agent builds its ivory record one graded transaction at a time.
